newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ super may start after NZ$9,000 earned - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ super may start after NZ$9,000 earned - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand's planned new compulsory superannuation system might allow the first NZ$9,000 of income and/or savings per year to be free from liability to the scheme, Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday.

"What we (the government) have talked about... is not just $5,000, which I recall was first mentioned, ...but also the additional sum of NZ$9,000, above which is set the current tax rate (threshold)," he said in answer to a parlaimentary question.
"We have talked about these options," he added.
At present income tax starts at a rebated rate of 15 percent on earnings up to $9,500.

It was agreed when the conservative National Party and the nationalist New Zealand First Party formed a coalition in December that a compulsory superannuation savings scheme, favoured by NZ First, would be put to public vote.
A referendum is scheduled for September.
New Zealand First proposed a retirement savings scheme that would eventually see at least eight percent of income diverted into pension savings.
If approved, it would come into force in July, 1998.
The government is currently working to finalise the exact design of the proposed scheme that will be put to the vote.
